newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends higher, boosted by late gains.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends higher, boosted by late gains.

text.p: COMEX copper ended higher, boosted by a late advance which helped prices break out of the narrow range which had dogged market for much of the session.
Most of the dealings were lackluster and thin.
But the red metal continued to be driven by good demand, particularly in the U.S., with trade hedge buying under the market giving support, William O'Neill of Merrill Lynch said.
Copper did not look overbought has already corrected itself twice in the past ten days. "It's been a very orderly type market -- copper has been the strongest metal in the LME complex," O'Neill said.
July COMEX copper settled 1.60 cents higher at 122.20 cents per lb, traded 122.30 to 120.70 cents. Spot June went out up 1.75 cents at 122.00 cents.
LME stocks continue to dwindle, falling 1,875 tonnes Monday to 123,775 tonnes, helping to keep the market at its best in over a year.
The LME cash to three months backwardation is also staying firm at $90/$95, providing another prop to prices.
Shipment delays still hinder Ok Tedi mine in Papua New Guinea, while the strike at Inco Limited in Canada continued into its third week.
